\section[a intenção]{a intenção — the intention}

\label{lesson:PT-C374-intencao}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for unlikely, then the Portuguese for the probability.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: a intenção}
\textbf{a intenção} — \textquotedblleft{}the intention\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Não tenho intenção de mudar de emprego.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{I have no intention of changing jobs.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Ter a intenção de} + infinitive. \emph{Com boa intenção} — meaning well.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{intenção} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{intentiō} \textquotedblleft{}a stretching out, a straining\textquotedblright{}, and later \textquotedblleft{}purpose\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short), from \emph{intendere} \textquotedblleft{}to stretch towards\textquotedblright{}, on \emph{tendere} \textquotedblleft{}to stretch\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{a intenção}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{a intenção}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{a intenção}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for unlikely, then the Portuguese for the probability, then say \emph{a intenção} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does a intenção mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The intention\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[o propósito]{o propósito — the purpose, the aim}

\label{lesson:PT-C374-proposito}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for the probability, then the Portuguese for the intention.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: o propósito}
\textbf{o propósito} — \textquotedblleft{}the purpose, the aim\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Qual é o propósito desta reunião?
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{What is the purpose of this meeting?}
\end{quote}

\emph{De propósito} — on purpose; \emph{a propósito} — by the way.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{propósito} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{prōpositum} \textquotedblleft{}a plan, a purpose\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short), the participle of \emph{prōpōnere} \textquotedblleft{}to set before\textquotedblright{}, on \emph{pōnere} \textquotedblleft{}to put\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{o propósito}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{o propósito}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for the probability, then the Portuguese for the intention, then say \emph{o propósito} again
\end{itemize}

\section[a meta]{a meta — the goal, the target; the finishing line}

\label{lesson:PT-C374-meta}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for the intention, then the Portuguese for the purpose.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: a meta}
\textbf{a meta} — \textquotedblleft{}the goal, the target; the finishing line\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
A minha meta é correr dez quilómetros.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{My goal is to run ten kilometres.}
\end{quote}

In a race, \emph{a meta} is the finishing line.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{meta} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{mēta} \textquotedblleft{}the turning post in a racecourse, a goal, a limit\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB, Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{a meta}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{a meta}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for the intention, then the Portuguese for the purpose, then say \emph{a meta} again
\end{itemize}

\section[disponível]{disponível — available; free (to meet)}

\label{lesson:PT-C374-disponivel}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for the purpose, then the Portuguese for the goal.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: disponível}
\textbf{disponível} — \textquotedblleft{}available; free (to meet)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Estou disponível na quinta à tarde.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{I am free on Thursday afternoon.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Estar disponível} — to be free; \emph{disponível em loja} — in stock.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{disponível} is built on \emph{dispor} \textquotedblleft{}to arrange, to have at hand\textquotedblright{}, from Latin \emph{dispōnere} \textquotedblleft{}to set in order\textquotedblright{}, on \emph{pōnere} \textquotedblleft{}to put\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short), with \emph{-ível}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for the purpose, then the Portuguese for the goal, then say \emph{disponível} again

\section[o compromisso]{o compromisso — the commitment, the engagement; the compromise}

\label{lesson:PT-C374-compromisso}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for the goal, then the Portuguese for available.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: o compromisso}
\textbf{o compromisso} — \textquotedblleft{}the commitment, the engagement; the compromise\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Hoje não posso: tenho um compromisso às seis.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{I cannot today: I have an engagement at six.}
\end{quote}

In Portugal \emph{um compromisso} is often an appointment or an obligation; it can also be a compromise.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{compromisso} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{comprōmissum} \textquotedblleft{}a mutual promise to accept a judge's decision\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), on \emph{prōmittere} \textquotedblleft{}to promise\textquotedblright{}, built on \emph{mittere} \textquotedblleft{}to send\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{o compromisso}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{o compromisso}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{o compromisso}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for the goal, then the Portuguese for available, then say \emph{o compromisso} again
\end{itemize}
